title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in SKU Product Detail Endpoint
description:
The /sku_product_detail.php endpoint accepts an 'id' parameter without any authentication or authorization checks. Any user (authenticated or not) can access product details for any valid SKU ID by directly modifying the id parameter in the URL. The application performs direct database lookups based on user-supplied ID values without verifying that the user has permission to view that specific product.

The vulnerability allows attackers to:
1. Enumerate all valid SKU IDs in the system
2. Access product details that may be intended for authorized users only
3. Map the complete product catalog through systematic ID enumeration
4. Combine this vulnerability with other findings (e.g., database schema enumeration via SSRF) to identify business-critical information

No role-based access control, ownership verification, or permission checking is performed before returning product details.
impact:
MEDIUM - The IDOR vulnerability in the product detail endpoint enables:

1. Unauthorized access to product details for any SKU ID without authentication
2. Information disclosure of business-sensitive product data (names, descriptions, SKU values)
3. Inventory enumeration - systematic mapping of all SKU IDs to identify the complete product catalog
4. Potential data exfiltration if product details contain sensitive business information (pricing, supplier data, internal notes, etc.)
5. Foundation for further attacks - once all product IDs are enumerated, they can be targeted in SQL injection tests or used to identify patterns in application logic
6. Competitive intelligence - competitors can enumerate the entire product catalog
7. When combined with the database details exposure vulnerability (visible IDs 12-19 in /sku_system.php), the enumeration surface is clearly defined
evidence:
POC Execution Output:

Test 1 - Access product ID 12:
- HTTP Status: 200 OK
- Response: ID: 12, SKU: TEST002, Name: test, Description: {{7*7}}
- Confirmed: Product data accessible without authentication

Test 2 - Access product ID 13 (different product):
- HTTP Status: 200 OK
- Response: Different product data (ID 13)
- Confirmed: Different IDs return different product information

Test 3 - Access non-existent product (ID 1):
- HTTP Status: 200 OK (processed without error)
- Response: "SKU not found" message returned
- Confirmed: Application still processes request, validating ID parameter exists

Test 4 - Enumeration of IDs 12-19:
- All IDs with HTTP 200 OK status
- Products found: IDs 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19 (7 out of 8 enumerated)
- Confirmed: Systematic enumeration is possible

Test 5 - No authentication required:
- Access with empty/no authentication headers: HTTP 200 OK
- Confirmed: No authentication checks are performed

Vulnerability Pattern:
- Direct parameter-to-database lookup (id parameter directly used in SQL query)
- No authentication verification before data access
- No authorization checks for user permissions
- No role-based access control validation
references: OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control, CWE-639 (Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key), CWE-284 (Improper Access Control), OWASP IDOR (Insecure Direct Object References)
toolCallDescription: Document the IDOR vulnerability in SKU product detail endpoint with confirmed POC showing unauthorized access to product information
